short_description: Consumer-facing appearance trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for inherited skin-pigmentation tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing appearance trait with practical raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited pigmentation tendency and current visible skin tone for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with broader inherited skin-pigmentation tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Skin pigmentation tendency is presented here as a cautious relative appearance signal related to inherited pigmentation, not as a direct readout of current observed skin tone in everyday conditions. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic readout of current observed skin tone.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Pigmentation traits are strongly population-structured, so this result should be interpreted as a panel-relative signal rather than a universal skin-color label.
Visible appearance can also shift with tanning, sun exposure, season, lighting, cosmetics, and photography conditions.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
